title: The needle for the next world
hook: tradition says Nanak gave rich Duni Chand a needle to return to him in the next world, and Duni Chand understood
tomorrow: Camp 2 close: one light, ten lamps

segments.voice: Yesterday, Bhai Kanhaiya, carrying water for the enemy. Your line was every face is his.
screen: `WATER FOR THE ENEMY — EVERY FACE IS HIS.`

segments.voice: Some people put their success on display: the car in the driveway, the watch that catches the light, the photos from the trip. In old Lahore, the story goes, a rich man named Duni Chand had a simpler system. On the roof of his house flew a row of flags, one for every hundred thousand rupees he owned, and the whole street could count them. One day Guru Nanak came to town, and Duni Chand invited him in, proud to host a holy man. Before he left, Nanak gave his rich host a gift. It was a needle.
screen: `THE CAR, THE WATCH, THE PHOTOS.` → `A FLAG FOR EVERY FORTUNE.` → `NANAK'S GIFT: A NEEDLE.`

segments.voice: This is one of the old janamsakhi stories, the life stories of Nanak that Sikhs have told for centuries. Nanak handed Duni Chand the needle and asked a favor. Keep this safe for me, he said, and when we meet in the next world, give it back. Duni Chand, eager to please, said of course. He took the needle to his wife and told her about the honor. She looked at him for a long moment. And how exactly, she asked, are you going to take a needle with you when you die? That landed. Duni Chand went straight back to Nanak. I can't do it, he said. Nothing goes with me. Not a needle. Not the flags. Then Nanak asked him, gently, the real question. If you can't take a needle, what will you take? The story says Duni Chand understood, and began to share what he had, giving it away to the hungry. Nanak doesn't lecture a rich man about money. He hands him one tiny object and lets him discover the rest, with a little help from his wife. In the Guru Granth Sahib, Guru Nanak says it plainly. Writing of wealth, he says, in paraphrase, that many have been ruined for its sake, and that it does not go with anyone who dies. What does go? Sikhs answer with the Name remembered, the honest work done, and what was shared. The flags stay on the roof.
screen: `KEEP IT, AND GIVE IT BACK LATER.` · `HOW WILL YOU TAKE A NEEDLE?` · `NOTHING GOES WITH ME.` · `THE NAME, THE WORK, THE SHARING.` · then, large: `WHAT GOES WITH YOU.`

segments.voice: Pick one thing you own, your phone, a ring, a mug, a jacket, and hold it or just look at it, thinking about how you got it, what it cost, and how much it matters to you. Then picture Duni Chand's wife asking her question: and how will you take this with you? No guilt needed; let the question sit beside the thing, then think of one thing in your life that could go with you.
Duni Chand. The rich man in Lahore who flew a flag for every hundred thousand rupees, and whom Guru Nanak gave a needle to keep until the next world.
Your line: what goes with you. Not the needle, not the flags. Ninety-five days in.
